1	# Betta.Abstractions
2	
3	> Same silhouette. Every fish is its own.
4	> Public SDK contract for authoring **Betta** plugins — zero-touch Grasshopper components from attributed C# service methods.
5	
6	This package contains only the attributes and interfaces needed to author a Betta plugin. The runtime (`Betta.gha`) is a Grasshopper plugin loaded by Rhino, **not** shipped inside your plugin DLL.
7	
8	## Quick start
9	
10	1. Create a class library targeting `net7.0-windows` (or any TFM that can reference `netstandard2.0`).
11	2. Reference `Betta.Abstractions` with `ExcludeAssets="runtime"` so your DLL doesn't redistribute a copy:
12	
13	   ```xml
14	   <PackageReference Include="Betta.Abstractions" Version="0.7.2.1"
15	                     ExcludeAssets="runtime" />
16	   ```
17	3. Define a service interface inheriting `IBettaCollection` and decorate it:
18	
19	   ```csharp
20	   using Betta.Attributes;
21	   using Betta.Interfaces;
22	
23	   [GrasshopperCollection("Strings", "Text")]
24	   public interface IStringCollection : IBettaCollection
25	   {
26	       [GrasshopperMethod("Upper")]
27	       string ToUpper([GrasshopperParameter("Text")] string text);
28	
29	       [GrasshopperMethod("Concat")]
30	       string Concat(
31	           [GrasshopperParameter("Left")] string left,
32	           [GrasshopperParameter("Right")] string right,
33	           [GrasshopperParameter("Separator")] string separator);
34	   }
35	
36	   public class StringCollection : IStringCollection
37	   {
38	       public string ToUpper(string text) => text?.ToUpper();
39	       public string Concat(string l, string r, string s) => l + s + r;
40	   }
41	   ```
42	4. Build. Drop the resulting DLL into `%AppData%\Grasshopper\Libraries\Betta\`. Restart Rhino — your components appear in the toolbar.
43	
44	## Attribute reference
45	
46	| Attribute | Target | Purpose |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| `[GrasshopperCollection(category, subCategory)]` | interface / class | Default Category + SubCategory for every method on the type. `FormerNames` lists the type's earlier full names, so saved files survive renaming or moving it. |
49	| `[GrasshopperMethod(name)]` | method | Marks the method as a Grasshopper component. Optional: `NickName`, `Description`, `Category`, `SubCategory`, `IconResource`, `Guid`, `FormerNames`, `Enabled`. The component's id is derived from the type and method name, so parameters and outputs can change (add new ones after the existing ones). After renaming the method, list its old name in `FormerNames` (`"Old.Namespace.Type.Name"` if it moved from another type) and saved `.gh` files keep working. `Guid` fixes the id instead, e.g. to port a hand-written `GH_Component` (keep its `ComponentGuid`). |
50	| `[GrasshopperParameter(name, ...)]` | parameter | Customizes input display name / nickname / description. List access is inferred from the CLR type (`List<T>` → list input). `DefaultValue = ...` seeds persistent data so unwired sockets carry your default. |
51	| `[GrasshopperOpaque]` | class / interface / method / `[return:]` | Opt the return type out of "explode into properties" — Betta ships it as a single typed wire via an auto-generated `Param_BettaGoo<T>` (deterministic ComponentGuid = MD5 of `T.FullName`). |
52	| `[GrasshopperRange(min, max)]` | parameter | Numeric range check; out-of-range surfaces a Warning + skips the invocation. |
53	| `[GrasshopperNotEmpty]` | parameter | Rejects null/whitespace strings and empty collections. |
54	| `[GrasshopperValidation(typeof(MyValidator))]` | parameter | Hands the value to your `IBettaValidator` implementation. |
55	| `[GrasshopperMenuState]` | parameter | Per-instance right-click menu state, not a wired input. Enum + bool get a right-click submenu. |
56	| `[GrasshopperSecret("service.key")]` | `string` parameter | Not a wired input. Value read from the OS credential store at solve time. Set via the `Betta_Secrets` Rhino command / GH menu. |
57	| `[GrasshopperTrigger]` | `bool` parameter | Not a wired input. Component adds a "Run" menu item; the method only fires when clicked. Method body can read the bool to distinguish manual runs from cache re-solves. |
58	| `[GrasshopperValueList("a", "b", ...)]` | parameter | Normal wired input, but Betta auto-attaches a `GH_ValueList` seeded with those items when the component is placed on the canvas. Skips inputs the user has already wired. |
59	| `IBettaReport` (parameter type) | parameter | Not a wired input. `report.Warning(…)` / `report.Remark(…)` show on the component while the method still returns its outputs; throw instead for an error with no outputs. |
60	| `[GrasshopperRequiresEntitlement("k")]` | method / class | Inert annotation. Enforced only when a plugin registers `IBettaLicenseGate` (see [Betta.Pro](https://github.com/KonradZaremba/betta.pro)); otherwise the method runs freely (OSS mode). |
61	
62	## Markers and module hook
63	
64	| Type | Purpose |
65	|---|---|
66	| `IBettaCollection` | The opt-in marker for plugin types — required on the interface (or the class for the no-interface style). |
67	| `IBettaValue` | Equivalent to `[GrasshopperOpaque]` on the class — marks a type as opaque so it passes through Betta wires as a single typed value. |
68	| `IBettaModule` | Optional hook: implement `void ConfigureServices(IServiceCollection)` to register your plugin's own DI services. Betta discovers + invokes every module before `BuildServiceProvider` at startup. (Runtime-dropped plugins do not get a module pass.) |
69	| `IBettaDefault` | Unwired opaque inputs get a fresh `new T()` instead of `null` when `T` implements this. |
70	| `IBettaSerializable` | Round-trip the opaque value through `.gh` save/reload via `byte[] ToBytes()` / `void LoadFromBytes(byte[])`. |
71	| `IBettaValidator` | Custom rule for `[GrasshopperValidation]`. Return null on success, error message on failure. |
72	| `IBettaLicenseGate` | Extension hook for entitlement enforcement. Register via `IBettaModule.ConfigureServices` — Betta consults it before loading each plugin assembly and before every `[GrasshopperRequiresEntitlement]`-gated solve. Ships in Betta.Pro; absent from a stock Betta install (OSS mode = every plugin runs freely). |
73	
74	## Custom icons
75	
76	Ship your own PNG as an embedded resource and reference it via `IconResource`:
77	
78	```xml
79	<EmbeddedResource Include="Resources\my_icon.png" />
80	```
81	
82	```csharp
83	[GrasshopperMethod("Foo", IconResource = "my_icon.png")]
84	double Foo(double x);
85	```
86	
87	The runtime matches `IconResource` against any embedded resource name **ending with** the supplied string, so the namespace prefix isn't required. Your PNG is rendered verbatim — no tinting, no overlay text.
88	
89	## License
90	
91	Mozilla Public License 2.0 — see the repository for details. File-level copyleft: referencing this package leaves your plugin code unaffected; only modifications to Betta's own source files must stay open.

# Betta.Abstractions

> Same silhouette. Every fish is its own.
> Public SDK contract for authoring **Betta** plugins — zero-touch Grasshopper components from attributed C# service methods.

This package contains only the attributes and interfaces needed to author a Betta plugin. The runtime (`Betta.gha`) is a Grasshopper plugin loaded by Rhino, **not** shipped inside your plugin DLL.

## Quick start

1. Create a class library targeting `net7.0-windows` (or any TFM that can reference `netstandard2.0`).
2. Reference `Betta.Abstractions` with `ExcludeAssets="runtime"` so your DLL doesn't redistribute a copy:

   ```xml
   <PackageReference Include="Betta.Abstractions" Version="0.7.2.1"
                     ExcludeAssets="runtime" />
   ```
3. Define a service interface inheriting `IBettaCollection` and decorate it:

   ```csharp
   using Betta.Attributes;
   using Betta.Interfaces;

   [GrasshopperCollection("Strings", "Text")]
   public interface IStringCollection : IBettaCollection
   {
       [GrasshopperMethod("Upper")]
       string ToUpper([GrasshopperParameter("Text")] string text);

       [GrasshopperMethod("Concat")]
       string Concat(
           [GrasshopperParameter("Left")] string left,
           [GrasshopperParameter("Right")] string right,
           [GrasshopperParameter("Separator")] string separator);
   }

   public class StringCollection : IStringCollection
   {
       public string ToUpper(string text) => text?.ToUpper();
       public string Concat(string l, string r, string s) => l + s + r;
   }
   ```
4. Build. Drop the resulting DLL into `%AppData%\Grasshopper\Libraries\Betta\`. Restart Rhino — your components appear in the toolbar.

## Attribute reference

| Attribute | Target | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `[GrasshopperCollection(category, subCategory)]` | interface / class | Default Category + SubCategory for every method on the type. `FormerNames` lists the type's earlier full names, so saved files survive renaming or moving it. |
| `[GrasshopperMethod(name)]` | method | Marks the method as a Grasshopper component. Optional: `NickName`, `Description`, `Category`, `SubCategory`, `IconResource`, `Guid`, `FormerNames`, `Enabled`. The component's id is derived from the type and method name, so parameters and outputs can change (add new ones after the existing ones). After renaming the method, list its old name in `FormerNames` (`"Old.Namespace.Type.Name"` if it moved from another type) and saved `.gh` files keep working. `Guid` fixes the id instead, e.g. to port a hand-written `GH_Component` (keep its `ComponentGuid`). |
| `[GrasshopperParameter(name, ...)]` | parameter | Customizes input display name / nickname / description. List access is inferred from the CLR type (`List<T>` → list input). `DefaultValue = ...` seeds persistent data so unwired sockets carry your default. |
| `[GrasshopperOpaque]` | class / interface / method / `[return:]` | Opt the return type out of "explode into properties" — Betta ships it as a single typed wire via an auto-generated `Param_BettaGoo<T>` (deterministic ComponentGuid = MD5 of `T.FullName`). |
| `[GrasshopperRange(min, max)]` | parameter | Numeric range check; out-of-range surfaces a Warning + skips the invocation. |
| `[GrasshopperNotEmpty]` | parameter | Rejects null/whitespace strings and empty collections. |
| `[GrasshopperValidation(typeof(MyValidator))]` | parameter | Hands the value to your `IBettaValidator` implementation. |
| `[GrasshopperMenuState]` | parameter | Per-instance right-click menu state, not a wired input. Enum + bool get a right-click submenu. |
| `[GrasshopperSecret("service.key")]` | `string` parameter | Not a wired input. Value read from the OS credential store at solve time. Set via the `Betta_Secrets` Rhino command / GH menu. |
| `[GrasshopperTrigger]` | `bool` parameter | Not a wired input. Component adds a "Run" menu item; the method only fires when clicked. Method body can read the bool to distinguish manual runs from cache re-solves. |
| `[GrasshopperValueList("a", "b", ...)]` | parameter | Normal wired input, but Betta auto-attaches a `GH_ValueList` seeded with those items when the component is placed on the canvas. Skips inputs the user has already wired. |
| `IBettaReport` (parameter type) | parameter | Not a wired input. `report.Warning(…)` / `report.Remark(…)` show on the component while the method still returns its outputs; throw instead for an error with no outputs. |
| `[GrasshopperRequiresEntitlement("k")]` | method / class | Inert annotation. Enforced only when a plugin registers `IBettaLicenseGate` (see [Betta.Pro](https://github.com/KonradZaremba/betta.pro)); otherwise the method runs freely (OSS mode). |

## Markers and module hook

| Type | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `IBettaCollection` | The opt-in marker for plugin types — required on the interface (or the class for the no-interface style). |
| `IBettaValue` | Equivalent to `[GrasshopperOpaque]` on the class — marks a type as opaque so it passes through Betta wires as a single typed value. |
| `IBettaModule` | Optional hook: implement `void ConfigureServices(IServiceCollection)` to register your plugin's own DI services. Betta discovers + invokes every module before `BuildServiceProvider` at startup. (Runtime-dropped plugins do not get a module pass.) |
| `IBettaDefault` | Unwired opaque inputs get a fresh `new T()` instead of `null` when `T` implements this. |
| `IBettaSerializable` | Round-trip the opaque value through `.gh` save/reload via `byte[] ToBytes()` / `void LoadFromBytes(byte[])`. |
| `IBettaValidator` | Custom rule for `[GrasshopperValidation]`. Return null on success, error message on failure. |
| `IBettaLicenseGate` | Extension hook for entitlement enforcement. Register via `IBettaModule.ConfigureServices` — Betta consults it before loading each plugin assembly and before every `[GrasshopperRequiresEntitlement]`-gated solve. Ships in Betta.Pro; absent from a stock Betta install (OSS mode = every plugin runs freely). |

## Custom icons

Ship your own PNG as an embedded resource and reference it via `IconResource`:

```xml
<EmbeddedResource Include="Resources\my_icon.png" />
```

```csharp
[GrasshopperMethod("Foo", IconResource = "my_icon.png")]
double Foo(double x);
```

The runtime matches `IconResource` against any embedded resource name **ending with** the supplied string, so the namespace prefix isn't required. Your PNG is rendered verbatim — no tinting, no overlay text.

## License

Mozilla Public License 2.0 — see the repository for details. File-level copyleft: referencing this package leaves your plugin code unaffected; only modifications to Betta's own source files must stay open.

content.text:
I added the eight Facade components and `dotnet build` succeeds with 0 warnings and 0 errors. I haven't loaded the plugin in Grasshopper, so none of the components have been run.

The code is in a new `Facade` folder. I left the old `Collection.cs` as it was.
- **`Panel.cs`:** a `Panel` class marked as an opaque Betta value, so each panel travels on its own "Panel" wire. It holds the four corners, index, outline, center, area, planarity deviation, and the width and height used for nesting and the cut list.
- **`PanelComponents.cs`:** Panelize Surface and Panel Info, under Facade / Panels.
- **`AnalysisComponents.cs`:** Planarity, Classify Panels and Panel Stats, under Facade / Analysis.
- **`FabricationComponents.cs`:** Group Identical Panels, Nest On Sheets and Cut List, under Facade / Fabrication.

Choices I made where the brief left room:
- **Panel index:** it is `u * vCount + v`, one number per panel.
- **Panel area:** half the cross product of the two diagonals, so it stays defined for panels that aren't flat.
- **Nest On Sheets:** it runs off the UI thread, cancels when the inputs change, and reports progress. A panel too big for an empty sheet in either orientation is skipped and counted in the "fit on no sheet" warning, without opening a new sheet for it.
- **Nest On Sheets output order:** outlines come out in placement order (tallest first), not input order.
- **Cut List:** it uses invariant-culture numbers rounded to three decimals.
- **Cut List write behaviour:** the CSV is returned whether or not Write is true. With Write true and an empty path it throws, so the component shows an error.
